The tests pass: the run exited 0 with 5 passed. That covers the new checks that page 1 returns items 0-9 and page 3 returns the last 5, and that pages 0, 4 and 99 still raise ValueError. I only ran the test suite and didn't run `python catalogue.py` itself. The CLI just calls `get_page`, so I expect it to behave the same.

The cause was `start = page * per_page` in `get_page`, which is 0-based. The validation and header were already 1-based. The fix is `start = (page - 1) * per_page`, so page 1 shows the first ten results and the last page shows the remainder.

One thing I noticed and did not change: `catalogue.py` prints the page header before calling `get_page`. A nonexistent page will print "Page 99 of 6" and then fail with a traceback. It is still an error, as you wanted, but you may prefer a cleaner message.

I can't file the mobile team's ticket, because I have no ticketing tool here and can't see their code. I've recorded it as a next step, and the draft from my earlier message is ready for you to paste into their tracker. I can't say whether their paging has the same bug.

         raise ValueError(f"there is no page {page}")
